user_decision.question: Pass 1 of task 136's required extraction series failed both documented ways: the systemd-unit path (model gemma4:cloud, the one actually wired to home.nix's configured model) had all 50 chunk-extraction calls fail with 'HTTP Error 402: Payment Required' from Ollama's cloud endpoint; the bare 'sapience sync' CLI silently falls back to a local llama3.1 model whose cold start did not finish a single chunk in 580 seconds. Neither path currently produces real findings. How should the extraction backend be fixed before the five-pass series continues?
options: Check and fix the Ollama cloud account/billing behind OLLAMA_API_KEY so gemma4:cloud (documented in home.nix as free) stops returning 402, then resume via the systemd-unit path
Switch programs.sapience.model to a different model confirmed funded/free on the live Ollama account, then resume via the systemd-unit path

Accept the local-only llama3.1 fallback (no cloud dependency) by passing --model llama3.1 --backend ollama explicitly, and verify in an uninterrupted run (ideally by the user, in an interactive terminal) whether it completes a pass in practical time
Pause task 136 until the extraction backend is confirmed working by some other means
user_decision.recommended: Check and fix the Ollama cloud account/billing behind OLLAMA_API_KEY so gemma4:cloud (documented in home.nix as free) stops returning 402, then resume via the systemd-unit path
user_decision.obligation: Makes at least one of the two ways this task's own dispatch names to run a hand-run pass ('sapience sync' or 'systemctl --user start sapience-sync.service') actually complete chunk extractions successfully, rather than failing every call or stalling indefinitely, so the required five-pass coverage series can produce real, non-zero coverage/pending deltas to measure.

errors.message: Bare 'sapience sync' (no --model flag) defaults to extract_local.py's own 'llama3.1' ollama-backend default rather than home.nix's configured 'gemma4:cloud', and cold-started a local single-threaded CPU llama-server that had not completed one chunk after 580 seconds.
errors.recommendation: Pass --model gemma4:cloud --backend ollama explicitly when hand-running via the bare CLI, or fix the CLI wrapper to pass it by default; alternatively run it uninterrupted in an interactive terminal to learn its real completion time.

memory_candidates.content: On this machine, sapience's two documented ways to hand-run a pass are not equivalent: systemctl --user start sapience-sync.service's deployed unit script passes --model gemma4:cloud explicitly, while the bare 'sapience sync' CLI wrapper passes no --model flag at all, so extract_local.py falls back to its own per-backend default ('llama3.1' for the ollama backend) instead of home.nix's programs.sapience.model. Always pass --model/--backend explicitly when hand-running via the bare CLI, or check which path is being used before trusting a coverage reading's timing.

sapience coverage's own summary line ('N chunks in 1 run') can look like a successful extraction while every underlying HTTP call actually failed (e.g. 402 Payment Required) -- the summary line counts attempted calls, not successful ones. journalctl --user -u sapience-sync is the authoritative source for whether a pass actually produced anything; check it before trusting coverage's timing or chunk count as a throughput signal.

sapience coverage's 'Ingested: ... across N repos' line lists repos with historical vault content from before any config change, not the live folder selection -- the 'Folders selected (N): ...' line is the authoritative live selection. Easy to misread the two as the same thing when a reconciliation just changed which folders are selected.
